name: Granular Corneal Dystrophy Type I

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Granular Corneal Dystrophy Type I

criteria.description: Presence of multiple discrete, sharply demarcated gray-white granular opacities in the anterior central corneal stroma
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the TGFBI gene (commonly R555W mutation)
Histological confirmation of hyaline deposits in corneal stroma on biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical corneal opacities plus either positive family history or confirmatory TGFBI gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is considered the gold standard for definitive diagnosis.

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing TGFBI gene mutation (commonly R555W)
Histopathology showing hyaline deposits in corneal stroma
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy demonstrating discrete granular stromal opacities
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing hyperreflective stromal deposits
genetic: Autosomal dominant mutations in TGFBI gene
other: Family pedigree analysis consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Amyloid deposits forming lattice lines rather than granular opacities
Presence of linear stromal opacities instead of discrete granules
Diffuse stromal haze with glycosaminoglycan deposits

redFlags: Recurrent corneal erosions refractory to treatment
Development of corneal ulceration or secondary infection
references: Klintworth GK. Corneal dystrophies. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2009;4:7.
Weiss JS, Møller HU, Aldave AJ, et al. IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies—edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
